text:
The cook evening stops
+before the table where you ate;
+and starving to death your memory comes
+tasting not even water, out of sheer sadness.
+
+      But, as always, your humility consents
+to being offered the saddest kindness.
+And you will not taste, for you see who comes
+filially to the table where you ate.
+
+      The cook evening implores you
+and weeps for you in its still-sordid apron,
+which begins to love us from hearing us so much.
+
+      I make an effort too; for there is no
+courage to help oneself to these birds.
+Ah! We are going to help ourselves to nothing now.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem XLVI — The Cook Evening Stops
translation.editorial_note: The mother’s absent table is sustained through culinary verbs; tarde cocinera remains the stark cook evening, and birds hover between food, omens, and the courage no diner possesses.
